input.quote: (b) Customer agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Kubient and its owners, shareholders, officers, directors, managers, agents, and employees from all third-party Claims arising out of or in connection with (i) Customer's unauthorized or inappropriate use of the Services, (ii) Customer's unauthorized or inappropriate use of the Auction Platform, (iii) Customer's breach of any representation or warranty under this Agreement, or (iv) the Content or Properties
input.rationale: Section 10(a) already gives us a broad, uncapped Kubient defence and indemnity for all third-party Claims arising out of or in connection with the Services, the Auction Platform, Kubient's breach of its representations and warranties (including its IP-ownership and compliance-with-Law warranties) and Kubient's acts or omissions, and Section 11 supplies the full notice / control / cooperation procedure — so the vendor side of the rule is materially satisfied at the preferred level (we do not seek the fallback's procure/modify/replace/refund menu or its 3x super-cap, which would be worse for us than the current uncapped indemnity). Two preferred elements fail: the indemnified group omits our affiliates, and our reciprocal indemnity in Section 10(b) is not narrow, extending to our use of the Services and Auction Platform, breach of any representation or warranty, and the acts or omissions of Customer and its contractors. We therefore add affiliates and cut Section 10(b) back to Customer-supplied Content/Properties and our own breach of Law, leaving Sections 10(a) and 11 otherwise untouched.

proposal.summary: Extend Kubient's indemnity to Customer's affiliates and narrow Customer's indemnity to Customer-supplied Content/Properties and Customer's breach of Law.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We extended Kubient's existing defence and indemnity to cover our affiliates, and narrowed our reciprocal indemnity to the Content and Properties we supply and our own breach of Law. Our preferred position is that the customer-side indemnity stay narrow; the balance of Section 10 and the Section 11 procedures are unchanged.
